newsitem.title: BELGIUM: W. Europe new car registrations seen rising in '97.
newsitem.headline: W. Europe new car registrations seen rising in '97.

text.p: New car registrations in western Europe are expected to rise by about two percent in 1997 from the previous year, a spokesman of the European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA) said on Wednesday.
"We said at the beginning of the year we expected about two percent growth for the overall market and we still think that will be about it," ACEA spokesman James Rosenstein told Reuters.

ACEA earlier said new car registrations jumped 9.3 percent in April to 1,272,100 units compared with the same month last year. For the first four months of 1997, the figure was 0.8 percent higher at 4,696,000 units compared with the same 1996 period.
The April figure was boosted by soaring sales in Italy as a result of a government incentive scheme. New car registrations in Italy jumped 52.4 percent.
"You never can tell what is going to happen with the incentive effect, how long this kind of growth will be sustained in Italy. Nobody can tell," Rosenstein said.
